title: The Gerund: What the Norm Accepts

sections.content: You know the gerund (*corriendo*) for actions at the same time from B1 Unit 2, and with *estar* from A1 Unit 19. The norm accepts it when it says how, while, or immediately before the main verb happens: *Leyó el informe tomando notas.* It rejects two uses that are common in speech and in the press. First, the gerund of a later action: *El tren salió a las ocho, llegando a las diez* should be *salió a las ocho y llegó a las diez*. Second, the gerund as an adjective after a noun: *una caja conteniendo libros* should be *una caja que contiene libros*. A gerund shows an action in progress, not a lasting quality of a thing. The norm keeps only two fixed phrases as exceptions: *agua hirviendo* and *un clavo ardiendo*.

sections.title: Accepted, and what replaces the rest
rows: She read the report taking notes. (at the same time)
Sacando la llave, abrió la puerta.
Taking out the key, she opened the door. (just before)
El tren salió a las ocho y llegó a las diez.
The train left at eight and arrived at ten. (later action: a finite verb)
A box containing books. (a que clause, not a gerund)

items.english: She corrected the text listening to music.

items.spanish: El avión despegó a las seis y aterrizó a las ocho.
items.english: The plane took off at six and landed at eight.

items.spanish: Recibimos una carta que contiene tres dudas.
items.english: We received a letter containing three queries.

items.spanish: Vi a Meg corrigiendo el texto.
items.english: I saw Meg correcting the text.

sections.content: English allows 'a box containing books' and 'he crashed, dying later', so both slip into Spanish easily. Ask two questions. Does the second action come after the first? Use *y* and a verb. Does the gerund describe a noun without an action in progress? Use *que* and a verb. The gerund is fine after a noun when you see or hear the action as it happens: *Vi a Meg corrigiendo el texto.*
